newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timor rebel says did not ask Mandela for release.
newsitem.headline: Timor rebel says did not ask Mandela for release.

text.p: Jailed East Timor rebel leader Jose "Xanana" Gusmao has said he did not ask South African President Nelson Mandela to push for his release from a 20-year jail term, Antara news agency reported on Monday.
After a state visit to Indonesia last month, Mandela sent a letter to President Suharto suggesting Gusmao be released to improve the prospects of a settlement to the East Timor problem.
Gusmao was quoted by Antara as saying on Sunday he did not ask Mandela to send the letter.
"(The request) is his own initiative," he said.
Gusmao was speaking to reporters at the Cipinang jail in east Jakarta during celebrations marking the 52nd anniversary of Indonesia's independence.

He is four years into a 20-year jail sentence for resisting Indonesian rule in East Timor, a former Portuguese colony that Indonesia invaded in 1975 and annexed the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Justice Minister Utoyo Usman said on Saturday Gusmao had been given a three-month reduction of his jail term for good conduct.
But Gusmao said on Sunday he did not need the reduction. "I don't need that," he said without elaborating.
Mandela last month secured Gusmao's temporary release and dined with him at the government guest house.
Government officials have reiterated that Gusmao is in jail for criminal offences and not because of his political beliefs.
